title: Uniqueness of Optimal Configurations for the Maximum-Angle Problem

problemStatement.formal: \text{For which } N \text{ is the extremal configuration attaining } \alpha_N = \min_{|P| = N}\ \max_{a,b,c \in P}\ \angle(a,b,c)\ \text{unique up to similarity?}
problemStatement.plain: Erdős Problem #504 (solved by Sendov, 1993) determines $\alpha_N$, the smallest achievable "largest angle" among $N$ planar points. The formula changes at the threshold $N = 5 \cdot 2^{n-3}$ within each dyadic interval $(2^{n-1}, 2^n]$, with two distinct optimal families. This sub-question asks: for which $N$ is the *optimal configuration itself* unique up to similarity (rotation, translation, scaling, reflection), and for which $N$ does a genuine one-parameter (or discrete) family of optima exist?
